brief.headline: Push toward ₹0.65–0.80/pc on the 28 mm PP cap (market shows headroom at higher volume) and offer 15-day faster payment (worth ₹2.77 L cash to us) in exchange for a matching price cut.

priceAsk.summary: Target ₹0.65–0.80/pc on the 28 mm induction-wad PP cap
priceAsk.basis: The open market for 28 mm induction-wad PP caps asks ₹0.55–1.20/pc, typically ₹0.85–0.95/pc. Market research shows modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume or looser spec — we should capture that.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Offer to pay 15 days earlier (15 days instead of current 30 days after receipt) in exchange for a price cut of similar value
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Paying 15 days faster costs us ₹2.77 L in cash tied up — we should recover that through a matching price drop.

brief.financialLeverage: Empire Industries does not publish financials, so we cannot see their profit or debt picture. That makes it harder to gauge how tight they are for cash. Our ₹67.47 L annual spend is real money, but without their revenue figure we cannot say how big a customer we are. The plan leans on our purchase data, the market ask, and lining up a second source to create credible walk-away pressure.

evidence.point: We spend ₹67.47 L a year with them on rigid plastic packaging — enough volume to justify better pricing
The market ask for 28 mm induction-wad PP caps is ₹0.55–1.20/pc, typically ₹0.85–0.95/pc, with headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume
HDPE resin import price sits at 87.61 ₹/kg — a public benchmark for raw-material cost trends
Paying 15 days earlier ties up ₹2.77 L of our cash — worth a matching price concession to them
We currently pay 30 days after receipt; moving to 15 days is a real benefit for their cash flow

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd (a lead to qualify — verify before RFQ)
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter, with pharma bottles and caps capability, revenue of ₹2569.83 Cr, and a health score of B (65/100) — the strongest second-source candidate on paper.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd (a lead to qualify — verify before RFQ)
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader for pails, containers, and pharma packaging — strong and profitable, a robust alternate for bottles and closures.

alternates.name: Hitech Corporation Ltd (a lead to qualify — verify before RFQ)
alternates.why: Listed moulded and blow-moulded packaging firm with broad capability across bottles and caps.

risks: Empire publishes no financials, so we fly blind on their cash position — if they are fragile, a hard squeeze could backfire; watch for signs of stress in lead times or quality.
The market-ask verdict is 'MARKET-FAIR' — our current price may already be reasonable, so the headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 depends on our willingness to commit higher volume or relax specs.
All three named alternates are leads from web research, not qualified sources — start RFQs now so we have real backup pricing before the next renewal.
Offering faster payment without a firm price-cut commitment locks in the cash cost with no guarantee of savings — make the trade explicit and conditional.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We want to keep this partnership strong — and with ₹67.47 L a year in business and the market showing room at ₹0.65–0.80 for this cap at volume, let's talk about how we get there together, especially if we can help your cash flow by paying faster.
